level.title: Elementary: city, travel, routines, health
goals: Find your way around a city
Describe routines and make future plans

lessons.title: Around the city (ESTAR)
lessons.learn: SER is for WHO you are; ESTAR is for WHERE you are. ESTOY = I am (located), ESTÁS = you are, ESTÁ = it is. La estación ESTÁ allí = The station is over there. Add IZQUIERDA (left) and DERECHA (right) and you can follow any directions.

grammar.title: ESTAR for location: estoy, estás, está
grammar.explain: ESTAR answers WHERE. ESTOY EN CASA = I am at home. Never use SER for location! Also learn CERCA (near) and LEJOS (far): Está cerca = It is near.
mistakes: Saying SOY en casa — location is always ESTAR.
Saying ESTÁ for yourself — I am = ESTOY.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
It is over there, on the right.
No, it is near. Five minutes.

lessons.title: Travel and the past
lessons.learn: Talk about finished trips with the PRETÉRITO (simple past). For -AR verbs: HABLÉ (I spoke), HABLASTE (you spoke), HABLÓ (he/she spoke). VIAJÉ A ESPAÑA = I travelled to Spain. One accent mark changes everything!

grammar.title: Past -AR: hablé, hablaste, habló
grammar.explain: Take off -AR, add -É (I), -ASTE (you), -Ó (he/she). Viajé = I travelled. These are finished, done actions: AYER (yesterday) loves the pretérito.
mistakes: Saying HABLO for the past — past I = HABLÉ (with accent!).
Forgetting AYER goes with finished past, not present.

lessons.title: Daily routines (reflexive verbs)
lessons.learn: Routines use REFLEXIVE verbs: the action goes back to you. ME LEVANTO = I get (myself) up. ME = myself, TE = yourself, SE = himself/herself. Every morning runs on ME/TE/SE!

grammar.title: Reflexive ME/TE/SE: me levanto
grammar.explain: LEVANTARSE = to get up. ME LEVANTO (I get up), TE LEVANTAS (you get up), SE LEVANTA (he/she gets up). The little word before the verb points back at the person.

examples.en: Do you shower in the morning?

mistakes: Saying LEVANTO without ME — it means 'I lift', not 'I get up'!
Mixing TE and SE: TE = you, SE = he/she.

dialogue.en: What time do you get up?

dialogue.t: Me levanto a las siete y me ducho.
dialogue.r: meh leh-VAHN-toh ah lahs SYEH-teh ee meh DOO-choh.
dialogue.en: I get up at seven and shower.
Yes, I have breakfast with my family.

lessons.title: Health and future plans
lessons.learn: At the doctor: ME DUELE LA CABEZA = my head hurts (to me it pains the head). For plans, Spanish loves IR A + verb: VOY A VIAJAR = I am going to travel. Easy future, no new endings!

grammar.title: Future with IR A: voy a viajar
grammar.explain: VOY = I go, VAS = you go, VA = he/she goes. VOY A + verb = I am going to…: VOY A COMER = I am going to eat. The second verb never changes!
mistakes: Changing the second verb: VOY A VIAJAR, never VOY A VIAJO.
Forgetting A: VOY A comer, not VOY comer.

dialogue.en: No, but I am going to rest.

lessons.title: Clothes and shopping (demonstratives)
lessons.learn: Shop in Spanish! LA CAMISA (shirt), LOS ZAPATOS (shoes). Point with ESTE (this, near me) and ESE (that, near you): ESTA CAMISA (this shirt), ESE VESTIDO (that dress).

grammar.title: ESTE vs ESE: this vs that
grammar.explain: ESTE/ESTA = this (near me). ESE/ESA = that (near you). They match gender: ESTE libro, ESTA camisa, ESE vestido, ESA tienda.
grammar.pattern: este/esta + near thing · ese/esa + farther thing
mistakes: Saying ESTE camisa — camisa is feminine: ESTA camisa.
Using ESE for things in your hand — near you is ESTE.

lessons.title: Weather and -ER/-IR past
lessons.learn: Weather uses HACER (to make): HACE SOL (it is sunny), HACE FRÍO (it is cold). Past of -ER/-IR verbs: COMÍ (I ate), VIVÍ (I lived), COMISTE, COMIÓ. Same endings for -ER and -IR!

grammar.title: Past -ER/-IR: comí, comiste, comió
grammar.explain: Drop -ER/-IR, add -Í (I), -ISTE (you), -IÓ (he/she). COMER → comí, comiste, comió. VIVIR → viví, viviste, vivió. Accents matter: COMIO (wrong) vs COMIÓ (he ate)!
mistakes: Forgetting the accent: COMIÓ, not COMIO.
Mixing -AR endings: COMÍ (not COMÉ) — -ER past I is -Í.

dialogue.en: It is sunny. Yesterday it rained.
